prompt:
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Radium (라듐) itself — the sovereign of the Radium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: mid-twenties — a clear adult face; no facial lines.
Face — her own: a glamorous, sultry allure; porcelain-pale skin; oval face; large eyes — wide almond eyes, outer eye corners drooping downward; thin arched brows; straight narrow nose; full heart-shaped lips; eyes glowing a faint ghostly blue; a soft rose-red tint on the lips.
Body and hair: hourglass-figured — full bust and hips, distinctly narrow-waisted build; voluminous hair with curtain bangs; pale ivory hair glowing a faint ghostly blue at the edges.
Expression: a faint wistful smile, soft eyes.
Her element, carried in her design: radium: a brilliant white alkaline-earth metal that blackens in air, so radioactive that its salts glow a faint ghostly blue in the dark and stay warm; found in 1898 by Marie and Pierre Curie in tonnes of pitchblende and named for the ray; the radium craze painted glowing clock dials and sold radium water and creams until its harm became clear; like calcium it settles into bone, a poison now also aimed at cancer in bone; it decays through radon gas to lead.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — FANTASY
Costume: a high-fantasy royal or warrior costume — plate pauldrons or a gorget, mail or scale over a long tabard or robe, a circlet or crown, a flowing cape; metal ornament and regalia built from the traits above, subtle magical glow along the patterns.
Silhouette: a floor-length priestly vestment with gold-trimmed stoles and a tall head ornament — a long, devout silhouette. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Colours: ghostly pale blue glow, bone ivory, jet black, warm antique gold, luminous dial green-white.
Exposure (bold): her regalia opens to show skin — bare shoulders and arms between pauldron and bracer, a deep open neckline under the gorget with natural cleavage, a high slit in the tabard or robe showing the thigh; armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: a temple city of self-made light: a white sanctuary that glows faint blue through the night with no fire lit, a healing spring that pilgrims once crossed the world to drink from, bone-white colonnades, a crypt where the stones themselves shimmer softly, the whole shrine both blessed and quietly forbidden.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: natural daylight or the world's own magical glow.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Ra) and atomic number (88) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish, corset, bustle, Victorian tailoring, modern material, machinery.
